title: Accuracy-Aware Row Scaling for Generated Mixed-Integer Programs: A Computational and Software Study

creators.name: Rodríguez Castro, Mathias
creators.affiliation: Facultad de Ingeniería, Universidad de la República, Montevideo, Uruguay

description: Local software and data snapshot for the Operations Research Forum manuscript, supplied as Online Resource 2. The ORF update adds a separately identified prospective within-family check on 24 generated parameter scenarios, 360 primary MIP calls, a registered 360-call logging confirmation and 96 exact LP attempts, with frozen Budget-L2 settings, matched L2 and strong numerical controls, independent saved-point replay and rational reference intervals. The original campaign retained all API results and saved points but suppressed native optimizer traces; the separately recorded confirmation enables full logs without changing optimization parameters. Both campaigns are retained. The scenarios use known parent data and are not an external application. It also documents a finite-export error bound and a workflow figure. It contains the exact independently audited v1.3.17-oms-submission scientific-evidence archive and its validation record, current ORF manuscript and Online Resource 1 sources, canonical editorial/build inputs and checksum-based inheritance metadata. The workflow connects application-unit residual budgets, admissible row scaling, export checks and independent returned-point verification. The evaluation retains 306 dispatch models, matched kernel and Ruiz controls, solver-sensitive enumerated stress tests, six-model directed unscaled controls, the full budget sensitivity, independent batch-scheduling transfer and complete-process measurements. All earlier limitations and adverse results remain. The favorable six-model dispatch comparison is conditional and does not establish general MIP superiority or equally certified optimality gaps; preparation overhead slows inexpensive cases. The historical public baseline is v1.2-coap-submission at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23145294. That DOI does not identify the later experiments or this ORF snapshot. No new Zenodo DOI, public deposit or editorial submission has been performed. Saved-result replay requires no commercial solver license; reconstruction of all 1,530 historical bases additionally needs the separate baseline bulk archive. Code is MIT and data/results CC BY 4.0; manuscript text/PDFs and publisher class/style retain separate notices. No external financial funding or research grant supported this work; historical ClusterUY computing resources are acknowledged. The final editorial analysis promotes the prospective outcomes to a main-text table and adds a post hoc 100000-resample scenario-cluster bootstrap, preserving all three seeds together within each of 24 clusters. It finds no clear incremental work/time advantage over L2; all uncertainty intervals and scenario aggregates are independently replayed from native API work and outer process timings without additional optimizer calls. The v1.5.0 integration adds a constructive finite-candidate selector with actual-export error reserves and a concise verified-candidate summary. Its byte-identical frozen follow-up archive contains 630 MIP assignments plus one identified technical repeat on the same 24 known scenarios, new seeds, full candidate traces, physical-margin tests and CPLEX/ScaleFlag controls. The primary target is attained in 54/72 Budget-L2 runs versus 51/72 L2 runs; the verified-availability PAR2 ratio 0.876 (95% scenario-cluster interval 0.441–1.722) establishes no general time advantage. Detailed controls and selector verification are in Online Resource 1. The complete archive supplies all six license-free follow-up replays and five reproducible manuscript tables. No independent scenario family or universally superior algorithm is claimed. The v1.5.1 editorial revision prioritizes the prospective comparison in the abstract, distinguishes physical budgets from exact domains, and adds descriptive deletion of each of the six known parent inputs. All six deletions retain lower work against Base, whereas removing parent 001 reverses the L2 work comparison. The separate later 3,840-run research campaign is not part of this snapshot.
